claims.text: When an Output<T> is used as if it were a plain value (e.g., in string conversion), Pulumi produces placeholder text like `Calling [toString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported` in log lines, generated files, or resource properties.
A page exists at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/output-values/ titled 'Output value errors' that describes this and other symptoms of treating an output as if it were already a plain value.
A Pulumi docs page exists at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/output-values/ covering errors from stringifying, branching on, or reading an output value like a plain value.
Pulumi Cloud/CLI can return the error "409 conflict: Another update is currently in progress" when an update is already in progress.
On Apple Silicon Macs, running x86_64 binaries under Rosetta 2 can cause Pulumi crashes or hangs.
Running `pulumi logs share` securely sends the logs from a failed operation to the Pulumi team.
The logging guide at /docs/iac/operations/debugging/logging/ has an 'automatic-logging' section.
A recently deleted stack can be recovered from the Pulumi Cloud console, including after an accidental `pulumi stack rm --force`.
Pulumi supports `--target` and `--exclude` flags to limit operations to specific resources.
The CLI produces `read ".pulumi/meta.yaml"` errors when it can't access a self-managed (DIY) state backend.
Pulumi Cloud can return 500 internal server errors.
Pulumi resource properties are represented as Outputs rather than plain values because their real values are not known until the providing resource has been created or updated.
Converting a Pulumi output value to a string directly instead of using apply does not raise an error by default; Pulumi silently substitutes a placeholder message in place of the value.

In TypeScript, the resulting string from string-converting an Output contains text such as `Calling [toString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported`, followed by guidance to use `apply` or `pulumi.interpolate`.
In TypeScript, calling `JSON.stringify()` on an output produces a `Calling [toJSON] on an [Output<T>] is not supported` string rather than the value.
In Python, formatting an Output into a string produces text such as `Calling __str__ on an Output[T] is not supported` and Pulumi also logs a warning, without raising an exception.
In Python, passing an output to `json.dumps()` fails with `TypeError: Object of type Output is not JSON serializable`; `Output.json_dumps()` should be used instead.
In Go, passing a `pulumi.StringOutput` where a `string` is expected is a compile error.
In C#, the resulting string contains text such as `Calling [ToString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported`, followed by guidance to use `Apply` or `Output.Format`.

Setting the environment variable `PULUMI_ERROR_OUTPUT_STRING=true` (supported in TypeScript, Python, and C#) makes string conversion of an output throw an exception instead of returning placeholder text.

The string-composition helpers are `pulumi.interpolate` and `pulumi.concat` in TypeScript, `Output.concat`/`Output.format`/`Output.json_dumps` in Python, `pulumi.Sprintf`/`pulumi.JSONMarshal` in Go, and `Output.Format` in C#.
An `apply` callback runs asynchronously once the output resolves, generally after the program's top-level code has finished running.
Most resource inputs accept outputs as well as plain values; a resource's logical name is a position that cannot accept an output.
In a dynamically typed language, an `if` on an Output object is generally always true because the output object itself is evaluated, not its eventual value.
In a statically typed language, branching on an `Output<bool>` is usually a compile error because an `Output<bool>` is not a `bool`.
Values known when the program starts, such as stack configuration read with `pulumi.Config`, environment variables, or hardcoded flags, are plain values and can be branched on normally.
Passing an output as a resource's logical name or loop bound fails to compile in TypeScript, Go, and C#.
In Python, passing an output as a resource's logical name raises `TypeError: Expected resource name to be a string`.
In Python, using an output as a loop bound (`range(some_output)`) raises `TypeError: 'Output' object cannot be interpreted as an integer`.
In Python, using an output as a dictionary key does not raise; it silently keys on the output object itself rather than its resolved value.
A StackReference lets a later, separate stack consume a first stack's outputs.
Pulumi has no supported way to block the program and synchronously pull a resolved value out of an output.
`pulumi stack output <name>` reads a single stack output from the CLI after a deployment.
The Automation API exposes an `outputs` field on the result of running an update (for example `res.Outputs` in Go).
